question:
Four squares of side length \(4,\) \(7,\) \(9,\) and \(10\) units are arranged in increasing size order so that their left edges and bottom edges align. The squares alternate shaded and unshaded, as shown in the figure. What is the area of the visible shaded region in square units?

[Figure 1](figures/2024_AMC_8_Q03_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Because the squares share their left and bottom edges, each smaller square fits inside the larger ones. The visible shaded pieces are the part of the side-\(10\) square outside the side-\(9\) square and the part of the side-\(7\) square outside the side-\(4\) square. These pieces do not overlap, so their areas add:
\[
(10^2-9^2)+(7^2-4^2)
=(100-81)+(49-16)
=19+33=52.
\]
The shaded area is \(\boxed{52}\) square units, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
